solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit grew with it

parts.note: past tense of rise, to grow or increase

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that some fruit grew alongside something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed pod left on a wild rose bush after flowering is a common fruit used in syrups.

clue.text: Notices I swerve all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters end up in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A driver admits to weaving erratically across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are critical write-ups of plays or books in the press, which are reviews.

clue.text: I run into lions scrambling for meat

indicators.note: scrambling mixes things up, so the combined letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone runs at a pride of lions scrambling for meat.
explanation.walkthrough: I and R join LIONS and the lot is jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a choice cut of beef from the loin, a kind of meat.

clue.text: Having a shock, perhaps, can be dangerous

definitions.meaning: first meaning: covered in hair, a shock being a thick mass of it
second meaning: risky or frightening, in informal use

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' suggests a fright or electric jolt, but here it is a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means covered in hair, such as a thick shock, and informally means risky or scary.

clue.text: Trunk, for example, for leader in charge held up

indicators.note: held means kept within the word for leader
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A tree trunk is propped up to support a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'up' reverses; 'held' puts the reversed abbreviation inside the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's trunk is a long nose, which zoologists call a proboscis.

clue.text: Fiasco as vehicle reversed by unqualified driver goes into river

indicators.note: the assembled letters enter and sit inside the river's name

parts.note: a river in Scotland, Wales and England

indicators.note: the vehicle's name is turned to run the other way round

parts.note: L for learner, as on the L-plate a learner driver displays

explanation.surface: A disaster unfolds as a learner backs a car into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain, so 'unqualified driver' is the letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, ignominious collapse or humiliating failure, exactly what a fiasco is.

clue.text: Manages to fit in small amounts of treatment

indicators.note: to fit in means the second word is slotted inside the first

explanation.surface: Someone squeezes in a little therapy where they can.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses are measured quantities of a medicine given at one time, portions of treatment.

clue.text: Captain and others showing effrontery to bowlers, maybe

parts.note: brass neck means cheek or nerve
a bowler is a hard round hat

explanation.surface: A cricket captain and teammates being cheeky to the bowlers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowlers suggests cricket, with a captain, but a bowler is a hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hats is slang for high-ranking military officers, with gold braid on their caps; a captain is one.

clue.text: Water container in restaurant in service area?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a soldier's or camper's flask
second meaning: a dining hall at a workplace, school or military base

explanation.walkthrough: Service area suggests a motorway stop, but the services here are the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a portable drinking flask and a dining hall for staff, pupils or soldiers.

clue.text: Drug abused in sect, say

indicators.note: abused means mistreated and knocked out of shape, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Narcotics are misused within a religious cult, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name of MDMA, an illegal recreational stimulant.

clue.text: After very short time, I bet, this'll make you dizzy

indicators.note: short means the word before it loses its last letter

parts.note: a go is a turn or stake in a game of chance

explanation.surface: A gambler boasts that their wager will soon leave you reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' only sets the order of the pieces; 'short' trims the word before it, not the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is the spinning, giddy sensation, so the condition is the thing that would make someone feel off balance.

clue.text: Bad marks in audition for place in London area

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: An actor's poor scores at a tryout for a London part.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a town on the Thames just west of London, near Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines-upon-Thames is a Surrey town on the western edge of Greater London's commuter belt.

clue.text: English horse, mostly quiet type, like Black Beauty

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a timid, quiet person, as in 'quiet as a mouse'

explanation.surface: Describing a quiet English horse, much like the famous one in the novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Beauty is both the novel's title and its horse, so the horse is the title's namesake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponymous character gives a work its title, as the horse Black Beauty names Anna Sewell's novel.

clue.text: Where some Italian citizens live — in Naples, i.e., Napoli?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the end of Naples, then i.e., then the start of Napoli

explanation.surface: A question of whether Italians live in Naples, that is, Napoli.
explanation.definitionFit: Siena is a Tuscan city, a home for some Italians.

clue.text: Import from various quarters once or twice

wordplay.note: compass points south, east, north, south, east: two used twice, one once

explanation.surface: Trade goods brought in from several regions now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are compass points; 'once or twice' says some points repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Import here is the noun meaning significance or gist, so the meaning of a statement is its sense.

clue.text: Criminal acts, for instance, including a lot of vile murder

indicators.note: including means the following letters are placed inside
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to do in is to kill

explanation.surface: Crimes, such as an appalling killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder' looks like part of the definition, but 'do in' is slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Evildoing is wicked behaviour or wrongdoing, deeds such as crimes.

clue.text: Unusually tiny trace, no doubt

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an unfamiliar way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddly small trace of evidence, beyond question.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty is something beyond question, a phrase meaning the same as no doubt.

clue.text: Ruling about head of state leaving office

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the other
head of points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A monarch's rule comes to an end as the head of state steps down.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigning is giving up a post voluntarily, quitting one's job or position.

clue.text: After my boss and I reorganised, is in a win-win situation

indicators.note: a reorganised group has its parts put in a new order

explanation.surface: An office restructure leaves both an employee and the manager happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts IS after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbiosis is a mutually beneficial relationship between two parties, where both gain.

clue.text: Rattles when it's false alarm

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the word's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Something shakes noisily when a bogus warning goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False alarm' reads as one phrase, but false is the signal and alarm the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to frighten or shock them suddenly, which is a close synonym.

clue.text: Game John reviewed in short publication

indicators.note: reviewed suggests looking back, so the name reads the other way
in puts the name inside the word for the publication

explanation.surface: A game John wrote up in a brief newsletter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah-jong is a Chinese tile game for four players.

clue.text: Precisely trace fishing-boat
Living in Manhattan, I'm a tenant

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of Manhattan to the start of tenant

explanation.surface: A renter explains they live in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Animate is an adjective for things that are alive, as opposed to inanimate objects.

clue.text: Having played successfully, there'll be a catch in it

definitions.text: Having played successfully, there'll be a catch in it

parts.words: Having played successfully, there'll be a catch in it
parts.note: surface reading: a sportsman wins and takes a catch, as in cricket

parts.words: Having played successfully, there'll be a catch in it
parts.note: setter's reading: an angler plays a hooked fish and lands it, then stores it in a net kept in the water

explanation.walkthrough: Playing a fish means tiring it on the line before landing it; anglers keep the catch alive until release.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepnet is a long mesh net in which anglers hold their live catch in the water.

clue.text: Small insect concealed on a plant, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A tiny bug lies hidden on a leaf at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places HID after A and P.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a tiny sap-sucking bug such as greenfly, a small insect pest.

clue.text: European saint venerated? Not out East

parts.note: the opposite of out, as a batsman still at the crease

explanation.surface: A revered holy figure from Europe who has not left the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Augustine of Hippo, or of Canterbury, was a Christian saint; the latter was Italian-born.

clue.text: For each person, it's in the future

parts.note: a as in 'ten pounds a go'
as in a charge per head

explanation.surface: A price per person to be paid at some later date.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means forward in time, still to come, so lying before us.

clue.text: Instrument — one embraced by George Harrison, for one

indicators.note: embraced means held in someone's arms, so this letter goes inside

explanation.surface: An instrument George Harrison of the Beatles famously took up.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrison really did learn the sitar from Ravi Shankar, so the surface is true.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed lute, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Practise deceit, like Disraeli as PM

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be unfaithful to a partner
second meaning: holding the office on two separate occasions

explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli was British Prime Minister twice, in 1868 and 1874-80.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means cheating on a lover, while the adjective describes someone holding an office for two separate terms.

clue.text: Rent home with American author

parts.note: Mark Twain, author of Huckleberry Finn

explanation.surface: Paying for lodgings shared with a writer from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent is the past participle of rend, to tear, not a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent means torn apart, and something split into two pieces is asunder in archaic phrasing.

clue.text: Romantically committed — having good time, in conclusion

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word for conclusion

explanation.surface: A couple are betrothed, having had a good time in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Being engaged means promised to marry, a formal romantic commitment before the wedding.

clue.text: Clobber bloke holding weapon

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the second inside it

explanation.surface: Hit a man who is carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber looks like a verb, to hit, but it is British slang for clothes or gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing, so an item of clothing is a garment.
